graph.title: LEGO City 60001 Fire Patrol Car (Fire Rescue)
notes: The two remaining groups are not a mistake. The booklet builds two separate models: the tree scene (page 4: jumper plate, trunk, leaves, with the cat and fish placed by it) and the fire patrol car (pages 5-27). No step joins the tree to the car, so I left them unconnected rather than invent a join.
The fish and cat belong to the tree scene. The fish only rests against the cat/minifigure (contact edge), and the cat rests on the leaves (contact edge).
Minifigures (fire fighter, woman) are not in the parts inventory, so they are not nodes. The radio is held by a minifig and only touches the tank brick (contact edge).
The sticker sheet (11843) is one node. Stickers go on the two side panels and the roof, so it has sticker-adhesion joins to those three parts.
All ports are left null. Stud and anti-stud contacts were read from small isometric pictures, so which exact studs are used is not recorded.

Some attachment targets are my best reading of the pictures. These are the red 1x4 plates in step 12, the blue seat panels, the white plates in steps 10 and 11, the hood parts in steps 17 and 18, and the windscreens.
Rear and front wheel arches are both joined to the base's end plates. Both brackets (14520) are joined to the base ends.

The two wheels on each wheel-holder plate are modelled as copies 1 and 2 on the first plate and copies 3 and 4 on the second, using attach overrides. Which plate is front and which is rear is not shown.
The 2431 tile in step 22 is listed as Trans-Dark Blue in the parts list, though the manual shows it as trans light blue. I used the parts-list colour.

graph_initial.title: LEGO City 60001 Fire Patrol Car (Fire Rescue)
notes: Minifigures (fire fighter, woman) are not in the parts inventory, so they are not nodes. The fish is held by the fire fighter and the radio by a minifig; the fish has no edges, and the radio only touches the tank brick.
The sticker sheet (11843) is a single node with no edges, because stickers are applied to many parts.
All ports are left null. Stud and anti-stud contacts were read from small isometric pictures, so which exact studs are used is not recorded.

Some attachment targets are my best reading of the pictures. These are the red 1x4 plates in step 12, the blue seat panels, the white plates in steps 10 and 11, the hood parts in steps 17 and 18, and the windscreens. The windscreens are modelled as joined to the red plates and then to the roof.
Rear and front wheel arches are both joined to the base's end plates. Both brackets (14520) are joined to the base ends.

The two wheels on each wheel-holder plate are modelled as copies 1 and 2 on the first plate and copies 3 and 4 on the second, using attach overrides. Which plate is front and which is rear is not shown.

In steps 12 and 13 the manual shows a blue 1x2 tile (3069b). The 2431 tile in step 22 is listed as Trans-Dark Blue in the parts list, though the manual shows it as trans light blue. I used the parts-list colour.
